dedupe_keys.name: owl i usa kilometer scale power outage dataset for the continental united states 2012 2024

description: Julian Rice and colleagues at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory publish OWL-I USA, nightly estimates of power-outage fractions derived from satellite night-time lights. Coverage is the continental United States from 19 January 2012 through 31 December 2024 at thirty-arcsecond resolution, approximately one kilometre. Annual NetCDF files are grouped into ten-degree tiles and include ensemble-mean outage fraction, ensemble standard deviation, estimated customers and LandScan population. The 2026 deposit is free under CC BY 4.0. Cloud-obscured nights lack estimates, and values are calibrated remote-sensing inferences, not direct customer-outage records. The authors report calibration against EAGLE-I; their accuracy claims were not independently tested. The series can support spatial outage-recovery and hazard-impact simulations within those limits. Related catalogue resources include EAGLE-I, LandScan and NASA Black Marble, which the metadata name as calibration, population or satellite-grid inputs. Archives were not downloaded.
